title: I Used the Library Study-Pod Booking Against the Group That Camped

parts.text: I arrived at pod 3 at 6:00 p.m. with a reservation and found a group that had been there since noon with jackets on extra chairs. The kiosk said my booking started now. I was twenty-two, midterms, holding a confirmation. They said they were in the zone. I photographed the kiosk, the jackets, and the noon backpack mound. Then I asked the desk to end the unbooked session, which is a button. At 6:07 the lights in pod 3 did the five-minute flicker the policy promised.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The flicker started and their jackets are still claiming chairs.

social.video_title: Noon campers in a 6 p.m. pod — Part 1/2
social.description: Midterms, jackets on chairs, in the zone. Desk had a button. Would you have found another pod?

parts.text: They left in a huff of chargers. I sat. The flicker stopped. Zone is not a reservation. Jackets are not people. I finished two problem sets. The kiosk liked my student ID. Camping is for tents. Pod 3 is for clocks. I unplugged nothing of theirs because they had taken it. The desk waved. Policy flickered so I did not have to yell. Yelling is for zones. Clocks are quieter.

social.video_title: The flicker did the eviction — Part 2/2
social.description: Chargers huffed out, problem sets done. Was a jacket a booking?
